memory_update.text: Prioritize ETN and GEV as the clearest US-listed direct OEM exposures to high-voltage grid equipment, transformer/switchgear demand, and data-center/grid electrification pull-through.
Add HUBB as a utility/substation/transmission component supplier with strong load-growth and grid-resiliency alignment, though high-voltage transformer specificity requires further segmentation.
Add POWL as a concentrated switchgear candidate; smaller and more cyclical than large-cap OEMs, but its medium-voltage switchgear and data-center opportunity language make it unusually relevant.
Add PWR as a second-order critical-path infrastructure platform, not a pure equipment maker; include for substation, transmission, and load-center execution bottleneck exposure.
DOE transformer lead-time evidence supports the node thesis that transformers and grid equipment can delay projects despite being a small share of total AI data-center capex.

Non-US or OTC-listed leaders such as Siemens Energy, Schneider Electric, Prysmian, Nexans, Hitachi Energy parent exposure, and Hyundai Electric were not included because this pass is limited to US-listed candidates; consider a separate global/ADR pass.

Cable and conductor exposure remains under-covered in this 5-name limit; potential future US-listed checks include Atkore, nVent, Mastec, MYR Group, and materials suppliers if the next pass expands beyond direct transformer/switchgear leaders.

node: High-voltage transformers, switchgear, cables, and grid-supporting equipment
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the high-voltage grid-equipment node. The strongest direct public-market mappings are electrical OEMs with transformer, switchgear, substation, power-distribution, or grid-solutions exposure, plus one critical-path grid construction/platform provider. The core chokepoint evidence is that DOE identifies transformer supply chains as a grid vulnerability with sharply extended lead times, while company filings show strong backlog/order momentum tied to data centers, utilities, grid modernization, and electrification. This is research-priority mapping only, not a trading recommendation.
